title: Addition and Subtraction to 20
seo_title: Grade 1 Addition and Subtraction Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Add to 20 and subtract from 20; use appropriate symbols (+, −, =); solve number sentences with a missing number; use doubling and halving.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 1 maths worksheets: addition and subtraction to 20, number lines, doubles, number sentences and missing numbers. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
key_big: Count on from the bigger number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Adding puts groups together; subtracting takes some away.
  • Count on from the bigger number: 8 + 3 → 9, 10, 11.
  • Count back to subtract: 12 − 3 → 11, 10, 9.
  • Doubles help: 6 + 6 = 12, so 6 + 7 = 13.

Examples

Example

9 + 4

9 + 1 = 10

10 + 3

Answer: 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the startStart counting on at the next number.
The wrong sign+ adds, − takes away.
The missing numberRead the sentence: what makes it true?

items.q:
Double 2.
2 + 2 = ?

Double 3.
3 + 3 = ?

Double 4.
4 + 4 = ?
items.e: 4 + 4 is a double. 4 + 4 = 8. A spider has 8 legs: 4 on each side.

items.q:
Double 5.
5 + 5 = ?
items.e: 5 + 5 is a double. 5 + 5 = 10. Two hands have 10 fingers: 5 and 5.

items.q:
Double 6.
6 + 6 = ?
items.e: 6 + 6 is a double. 6 + 6 = 12. An egg carton has 2 rows of 6 eggs: 12 eggs.

items.q:
Double 7.
7 + 7 = ?
items.e: 7 + 7 is a double. 7 + 7 = 14. Two weeks have 14 days: 7 and 7.

items.q:
Double 8.
8 + 8 = ?
items.e: 8 + 8 is a double. 8 + 8 = 16. 8 + 2 = 10, and 6 more is 16.

items.q:
Double 9.
9 + 9 = ?
items.e: 9 + 9 is a double. 9 + 9 = 18. 10 + 10 = 20. Take away 2, and you get 18.

items.q:
Use a double.
2 + 3 = ?
items.e: 2 + 2 = 4. 3 is 1 more than 2, so add 1 more: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q:
Use a double.
3 + 4 = ?
items.e: 3 + 3 = 6. 4 is 1 more than 3, so add 1 more: 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 9 balls. 4 are crossed out, so take away. 5 are left. 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 7 fish. 2 are crossed out, so take away. 5 are left. 7 − 2 = 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 10 apples. 3 are crossed out, so take away. 7 are left. 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the ten frames?
items.e: 10 red counters and 4 green counters. Put them together: 10 + 4 = 14.

items.e: The jump starts at 8. It goes back 3 and lands on 5. 8 − 3 = 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jump?
items.e: The jump starts at 6. It goes on 5 and lands on 11. 6 + 5 = 11.

items.q:
Start at 5. Count on 3.
5 + 3 = ?
items.e: Start at 5. Count on 3: 6, 7, 8. Do not count the 5. 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q:
Start at 8. Count on 4.
8 + 4 = ?
items.e: Start at 8. Count on 4: 9, 10, 11, 12. Do not count the 8. 8 + 4 = 12.

items.q:

9 + 5 = ?

items.q:

items.q:

items.q:

9 − 3 = ?

items.q:

items.q:

items.q:
Start at 11. Count back 5.
11 − 5 = ?

items.q:
Start on 7. How many jumps to 12?
7 + ? = 12
items.e: Start on 7. Count the jumps to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5 jumps. 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q:
Start on 6. How many jumps to 13?
6 + ? = 13
items.e: Start on 6. Count the jumps to 13: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 7 jumps. 6 + 7 = 13.

items.q:
How many balls are crossed out?
11 − ? = 7
items.e: 4 are crossed out. 11 − 4 = 7. The missing number is 4.
